cards.title: console.log() prints
cards.body: `console.log()` shows a value in the console, the text window where programs print. Text goes in quotes.

hi.title: console.log() print karta hai
hi.body: `console.log()` console mein ek value dikhata hai, yaani woh text window jahan programs print karte hain. Text quotes mein jaata hai.

cards.title: One line each
cards.body: Each `console.log()` prints on its own line. The semicolon at the end marks the end of a statement.

hi.title: Har ek apni line par
hi.body: Har `console.log()` apni alag line par print karta hai. Aakhir ka semicolon batata hai ki statement yahan khatam hua.

cards.title: Every character counts
cards.body: The grader compares your output letter by letter, so capitals, commas and spaces all matter. `Hello` and `hello` are different.

hi.title: Har character matter karta hai
hi.body: Grader aapka output letter by letter compare karta hai, isliye capitals, commas aur spaces sab matter karte hain. `Hello` aur `hello` alag hain.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: One of these lines crashes with a `TypeError`. Tap it.

bug.fix: JavaScript cares about capitals: it is `console.log`, not `console.Log`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Inmein se ek line `TypeError` dekar crash hoti hai. Us par tap karo.
hi.fix: JavaScript capitals ka dhyan rakhta hai: sahi hai `console.log`, `console.Log` nahi.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: `+` joins the two strings exactly as they are, then `console.log()` prints the result without quotes.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: `+` dono strings ko bilkul waise hi jodta hai jaise woh hain, phir `console.log()` result ko bina quotes ke print karta hai.

exercise.prompt: Every programmer starts here. Print exactly `Hello, JavaScript!`
exercise.promptHi: Har programmer yahin se shuru karta hai. Bilkul `Hello, JavaScript!` print karo.
